chunks: And by this chain of transmission, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about performing voluntary prayer (tatatawwu') during the day while I was traveling.
He said: No. But you may make up the night prayer during the day while you are traveling.
I said: May I be your ransom — [what about] the daytime prayers that I perform at home; may I make them up during the day while traveling?
He said: As for me, I do not make them up.

key_terms.أَقْضِيهَا: To make up (qadā'); the performance of a missed prayer outside its originally prescribed time
key_terms.التَّطَوُّعِ: Voluntary/supererogatory worship; here specifically the nawafil prayers performed beyond the obligatory (fard) prayers
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Travel (safar); a defined legal category in Islamic jurisprudence that suspends or modifies certain prayer obligations
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: Home/residence (hadar); the state of non-travel, the legal counterpart to al-safar
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer (salat al-layl); the supererogatory nawafil of the night, whose qadā' is here explicitly permitted during daytime travel

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Rida (AS), can a traveler perform new voluntary prayers or make up missed daytime nawafil during the day while traveling?
ai.summary: Safwan ibn Yahya, one of the most trusted companions of Imam al-Rida (AS), poses two distinct questions about supererogatory prayer during travel: first, whether new voluntary (tatatawwu') prayers may be performed during the day on a journey, and second, whether daytime nawafil customarily prayed at home may be made up (qadā') while traveling. The Imam prohibits new daytime tatatawwu' in travel, permits the qadā' of the night prayer during daytime travel, and then answers the second question by stating his own personal practice — he does not make up the daytime nawafil — which in Shia jurisprudence functions as an authoritative normative ruling.
